title: Aśoka and the Decline of the Mauryas
author: Romila Thapar
note: The classic study of Ashoka's reign and the edicts; the source of the long-running debate on what dhamma meant.

title: The Mauryas Revisited
author: Romila Thapar
note: Thapar's later lectures, which revise her own earlier picture of a highly centralised state.

title: Early India: From the Origins to AD 1300
author: Romila Thapar
note: A readable survey; the Mauryan chapters are a good next step after this page.

title: A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India: From the Stone Age to the 12th Century
author: Upinder Singh
note: A textbook that sets out the evidence (inscriptions, coins, archaeology, texts) alongside the narrative.

title: Ashoka in Ancient India
author: Nayanjot Lahiri
note: A biography of Ashoka built closely on the inscriptions and the places where they were set up.

title: King, Governance, and Law in Ancient India: Kauṭilya's Arthaśāstra
author: Patrick Olivelle (translator)
note: A modern English translation of the Arthashastra, with an introduction on when and how the text was composed.

title: Inscriptions of Asoka (Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. I, new edition)
author: E. Hultzsch
publisher: Clarendon Press, for the Government of India
note: The standard older edition of the edicts, with texts and English translations. Out of copyright in many countries; check before reusing.

title: Ancient India as Described by Megasthenes and Arrian
author: J. W. McCrindle (translator)
note: English translation of the surviving fragments of Megasthenes' Indica, as quoted by later Greek and Roman writers.

title: Who We Are and How We Got Here: Ancient DNA and the New Science of the Human Past
author: David Reich
note: A geneticist's account of ancient-DNA findings, with a chapter on South Asia.

title: The formation of human populations in South and Central Asia
author: Vagheesh M. Narasimhan and others
note: The large 2019 ancient-DNA study most often cited in the migration debate.

title: The Quest for the Origins of Vedic Culture: The Indo-Aryan Migration Debate
author: Edwin Bryant
note: Sets out the arguments of both sides, including Indian scholars who reject migration.

title: The Rigveda: A Historical Analysis
author: Shrikant G. Talageri
note: A leading statement of the view that Vedic culture originated inside India.

title: The Horse, the Wheel, and Language: How Bronze-Age Riders from the Eurasian Steppes Shaped the Modern World
author: David W. Anthony
note: The archaeological case for a steppe origin of the Indo-European languages.

title: Early Indians: The Story of Our Ancestors and Where We Came From
author: Tony Joseph
note: A readable introduction to the genetic evidence for general readers.

title: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
author: Dadabhai Naoroji
note: The classic statement of the “drain of wealth” argument, by an early nationalist leader.

title: The Economic History of India under Early British Rule
author: Romesh Chunder Dutt
note: A nationalist economic history arguing that British policy harmed Indian industry and agriculture.

title: The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India
author: Bipan Chandra
note: A history of the drain argument and the early nationalists who made it.

title: Towards a Reinterpretation of Nineteenth-Century Indian Economic History
author: Morris D. Morris
note: An influential challenge to the nationalist account, which started a long exchange with Indian historians.

title: The Economic History of India, 1857–1947
author: Tirthankar Roy
note: A standard textbook that weighs both colonial costs and the changes of the period.

title: Trading Encounters: From the Euphrates to the Indus in the Bronze Age
author: Shereen Ratnagar
note: The main study of trade between the Indus cities and Mesopotamia.

title: The Indus Civilization: A Contemporary Perspective
author: Gregory L. Possehl
note: A survey of the Indus civilisation, including its contacts to the west.

title: Ancient Cities of the Indus Valley Civilization
author: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer
note: An illustrated introduction by an archaeologist who has excavated at Harappa.

title: The Periplus Maris Erythraei: Text with Introduction, Translation, and Commentary
author: Lionel Casson (translator)
note: A first-century CE Greek sailing guide to the ports of the Red Sea, Arabia and India.

title: Rome and the Distant East: Trade Routes to the Ancient Lands of Arabia, India and China
author: Raoul McLaughlin
note: A readable account of Roman trade with India and beyond.

title: Arikamedu: An Indo-Roman Trading-Station on the East Coast of India
author: R. E. M. Wheeler, A. Ghosh and Krishna Deva
note: The excavation report on Arikamedu, near Puducherry.

title: The Oxford Introduction to Proto-Indo-European and the Proto-Indo-European World
author: J. P. Mallory and D. Q. Adams
note: The standard reference on the shared vocabulary of the Indo-European languages.

title: Mathematics in India
author: Kim Plofker
note: The standard modern history of Indian mathematics, careful about dates and attributions.

title: The Universal History of Numbers
author: Georges Ifrah
note: A wide survey of number systems; some of its claims are disputed by specialists.

title: Algebra, with Arithmetic and Mensuration, from the Sanscrit of Brahmegupta and Bháscara
author: Henry Thomas Colebrooke (translator)
note: An early English translation of Brahmagupta's arithmetic, including his rules for zero.

title: The Āryabhaṭīya of Āryabhaṭa
author: Walter Eugene Clark (translator)
note: English translation of Aryabhata's work of 499 CE.

title: Fibonacci's Liber Abaci: A Translation into Modern English
author: Laurence Sigler (translator)
note: Fibonacci's 1202 book, which opens by teaching the nine Indian figures and zero.

title: Gaṇita-Yukti-Bhāṣā (Rationales in Mathematical Astronomy) of Jyeṣṭhadeva
author: K. V. Sarma, K. Ramasubramanian, M. D. Srinivas and M. S. Sriram (translators)
note: Translation of the 16th-century Malayalam text that sets out the Kerala school's infinite series.

title: The so-called Fibonacci numbers in ancient and medieval India
author: Parmanand Singh
note: Traces the sequence through Sanskrit and Prakrit writers on poetic metre.

title: An English Translation of the Sushruta Samhita
author: Kaviraj Kunja Lal Bhishagratna (translator)
note: Early English translation of the Sushruta Samhita, published in volumes from 1907.

title: An Account of Two Successful Operations for Restoring a Lost Nose from the Integuments of the Forehead
author: J. C. Carpue
note: Carpue's report of his operations, which he based on the Indian method.

title: First evidence of cotton at Neolithic Mehrgarh, Pakistan: analysis of mineralized fibres from a copper bead
author: Christophe Moulherat and others
note: The study that identified cotton fibres preserved inside a copper bead from a Mehrgarh burial.

title: Sweetness and Power: The Place of Sugar in Modern History
author: Sidney W. Mintz
note: A history of sugar, including its early history in India and its spread west.

title: India's Legendary Wootz Steel: An Advanced Material of the Ancient World
author: Sharada Srinivasan and Srinivasa Ranganathan
publisher: National Institute of Advanced Studies and Indian Institute of Science
note: Archaeological and metallurgical study of South Indian crucible steel.

title: A History of Chess
author: H. J. R. Murray
note: The classic history of chess, tracing it to the Indian game chaturanga.

title: The Art of Play: Board and Card Games of India
author: Andrew Topsfield (editor)
note: Essays on Indian games, including the moral board game that became snakes and ladders.

title: The Yoga Sūtras of Patañjali
author: Edwin F. Bryant (translator)
note: Translation with a long introduction on the text's date and background.

title: A critical study of the work “Vyamanika Shastra”
author: H. S. Mukunda, S. M. Deshpande, H. R. Nagendra, A. Prabhu and S. P. Govindaraju
note: The study by engineers at the Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, which found the designs could not fly.

title: The Satapatha-Brahmana, Part I (Sacred Books of the East, vol. 12)
author: Julius Eggeling (translator)
note: English translation that includes the story of Manu and the fish (Book 1, chapter 8).

title: The Ancient Indus: Urbanism, Economy, and Society
author: Rita P. Wright
note: A survey of Indus cities, farming, crafts and trade, built on recent excavation.

title: The Ancient Indus Valley: New Perspectives
author: Jane R. McIntosh
note: An accessible overview of the civilisation, its rise and its decline.

title: Deciphering the Indus Script
author: Asko Parpola
note: The fullest case for reading the script as an early Dravidian language.

title: The Collapse of the Indus-Script Thesis: The Myth of a Literate Harappan Civilization
author: Steve Farmer, Richard Sproat and Michael Witzel
publisher: Electronic Journal of Vedic Studies, vol. 11
note: A contested argument that the Indus signs were not a full writing system.

title: An ancient Harappan genome lacks ancestry from steppe pastoralists or Iranian farmers
author: Vasant Shinde and others
note: The first published ancient genome from an Indus site, from Rakhigarhi.

title: Inscriptions of the Early Gupta Kings and Their Successors (Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. III)
author: John Faithfull Fleet
note: Texts and translations of Gupta inscriptions, including Samudragupta's Allahabad pillar.

title: A Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms: Being an Account by the Chinese Monk Fâ-Hien of His Travels in India and Ceylon
author: James Legge (translator)
note: Translation of Faxian's account of his journey through India in the early 400s CE.

title: Rise and Fall of the Imperial Guptas
author: Ashvini Agrawal
note: A political history of the Gupta dynasty built on inscriptions and coins.

title: Ajanta: History and Development, Volume 1: The End of the Golden Age
author: Walter M. Spink
note: The first volume of Spink's detailed study, which dates the later Ajanta caves to the Vakataka king Harishena.

title: Delhi Iron Pillar: New Insights
author: R. Balasubramaniam
publisher: Indian Institute of Advanced Study and Aryan Books International
note: A metallurgist's study of the pillar's inscription and its resistance to rust.

title: The Mughal Empire (The New Cambridge History of India, I.5)
author: John F. Richards
note: The standard one-volume history of the empire.

title: The Agrarian System of Mughal India, 1556–1707
author: Irfan Habib
note: A classic study of land revenue and peasant life, which argued that heavy extraction fed the empire's crisis.

title: The Mughal State, 1526–1750
author: Muzaffar Alam and Sanjay Subrahmanyam (editors)
note: Essays on how historians have understood the Mughal state, including the debate on its decline.

title: The Baburnama: Memoirs of Babur, Prince and Emperor
author: Wheeler M. Thackston (translator)
publisher: Freer Gallery of Art and Oxford University Press
note: Babur's own memoir, in a modern English translation.

title: The Ain i Akbari by Abul Fazl Allami, Vol. I
author: H. Blochmann (translator)
note: Translation of the official account of Akbar's government, written by his minister Abu'l Fazl.

title: Aurangzeb: The Life and Legacy of India's Most Controversial King
author: Audrey Truschke
note: A short, much-debated reassessment of Aurangzeb's reign.

title: The Complete Taj Mahal and the Riverfront Gardens of Agra
author: Ebba Koch
note: An architectural historian's study of the Taj Mahal and Mughal Agra.

title: The Marathas, 1600–1818 (The New Cambridge History of India, II.4)
author: Stewart Gordon
note: A history of the Maratha state from Shivaji to its defeat by the British.

title: From Plassey to Partition: A History of Modern India
author: Sekhar Bandyopadhyay
note: A widely used textbook covering the whole colonial period and its historiography.

title: Indian Society and the Making of the British Empire (The New Cambridge History of India, II.1)
author: C. A. Bayly
note: On how Company rule grew out of, and changed, eighteenth-century Indian society.

title: India's Struggle for Independence, 1857–1947
author: Bipan Chandra and others
note: A narrative history of the national movement.

title: Modern India, 1885–1947
author: Sumit Sarkar
note: A history of the period that gives weight to peasants, workers and regional movements.

title: Awadh in Revolt, 1857–1858: A Study of Popular Resistance
author: Rudrangshu Mukherjee
note: Shows how the 1857 rising in Awadh drew in peasants and landholders, not only soldiers.

title: Late Victorian Holocausts: El Niño Famines and the Making of the Third World
author: Mike Davis
note: A polemical history of the late nineteenth-century famines and colonial policy.

title: Elementary Aspects of Peasant Insurgency in Colonial India
author: Ranajit Guha
note: A founding work of subaltern studies.

title: Hind Swaraj, or Indian Home Rule
author: M. K. Gandhi
note: Gandhi's short early statement of his ideas on self-rule and modern civilisation.

title: The Indian War of Independence of 1857
author: V. D. Savarkar
note: The nationalist reinterpretation of 1857 as a war of independence; banned in British India.

title: The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857
author: R. C. Majumdar
note: A leading nationalist historian who nonetheless argued that 1857 was not a national war of independence.

title: Eighteen Fifty-Seven
author: Surendra Nath Sen
note: The official centenary history, commissioned by the Government of India.

title: The Peasant Armed: The Indian Revolt of 1857
author: Eric Stokes
note: A district-by-district study of who joined the revolt, and why.

title: Temple Desecration and Indo-Muslim States
author: Richard M. Eaton
note: Catalogues documented cases of temple destruction and argues they were mainly political acts.

title: India in the Persianate Age, 1000–1765
author: Richard M. Eaton
note: A history of the period that stresses shared Persianate and Sanskrit cultures.

title: The History and Culture of the Indian People, Vol. VI: The Delhi Sultanate
author: R. C. Majumdar (general editor)
note: Part of a multi-volume nationalist history that emphasises conquest and resistance.

title: Hindu Temples: What Happened to Them
author: Sita Ram Goel and others
note: A list-based case that temple destruction was widespread and religiously motivated.

title: History of Aurangzib, Vol. I
author: Jadunath Sarkar
note: A classic multi-volume history, built on Persian sources, that portrays Aurangzeb as a bigot whose policies ruined the empire.

title: The Rigveda: The Earliest Religious Poetry of India
author: Stephanie W. Jamison and Joel P. Brereton (translators)
note: A complete modern translation, with an introduction on the text's date and setting.

title: The Sanskrit Epics
author: John Brockington
note: A survey of scholarship on how the Mahabharata and Ramayana grew over centuries.

title: The Sarasvati Flows On: The Continuity of Indian Culture
author: B. B. Lal
note: A senior archaeologist's case for continuity from the Harappans to Vedic culture.

title: The Past Before Us: Historical Traditions of Early North India
author: Romila Thapar
note: Argues that early India had many forms of historical writing, from genealogies to chronicles.

title: Kalhaṇa's Rājataraṅgiṇī: A Chronicle of the Kings of Kaśmīr
author: M. A. Stein (translator)
note: Translation of Kalhana's twelfth-century verse history of Kashmir.

title: The History of British India
author: James Mill
note: An influential colonial history that divided India's past into Hindu, Muslim and British periods, and dismissed Indian civilisation.

title: Berenike and the Ancient Maritime Spice Route
author: Steven E. Sidebotham
note: The excavator of Berenike, a Red Sea port, on its trade with India.

title: From Cyrus to Alexander: A History of the Persian Empire
author: Pierre Briant
note: The standard history of the Achaemenid empire, including its Indian provinces.

title: Herodotus, Vol. II: Books III–IV (Loeb Classical Library)
author: A. D. Godley (translator)
note: Book III lists the tribute of the Persian provinces, including the Indians.

title: Si-Yu-Ki: Buddhist Records of the Western World
author: Samuel Beal (translator)
note: Translation of Xuanzang's record of his journey through Central Asia and India.

title: Buddhism, Diplomacy, and Trade: The Realignment of Sino-Indian Relations, 600–1400
author: Tansen Sen
note: How exchanges between India and China changed from Buddhist pilgrimage to trade.

title: The Buddhist Conquest of China
author: Erik Zürcher
note: The classic study of how Buddhism took root in early medieval China.

title: The Indianized States of Southeast Asia
author: George Cœdès
note: The classic, now much-criticised, account of Indian influence on early Southeast Asian kingdoms.

title: History, Culture, and Region in Southeast Asian Perspectives
author: O. W. Wolters
note: Argues that Southeast Asian societies adapted Indian ideas for their own purposes (“localization”).

title: Nagapattinam to Suvarnadwipa: Reflections on the Chola Naval Expeditions to Southeast Asia
author: Hermann Kulke, K. Kesavapany and Vijay Sakhuja (editors)
note: Essays on the Chola raid on Srivijaya around 1025 CE and its context.
